from.place: Strict flat-model normalization: only the scalar-cokernel quasi-isomorphism field

title: Scalar cokernels of strict finite flat DVR models
statement: Let T be a normalized DVR tower [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. Choose finite-coefficient complexes P_j with flat terms, K-flat in the sense of [def-pc-kflat-complex], isomorphisms Q(P_j) ≅ T.M j, and semilinear successor chain maps representing its transitions. Restrict P_j to completed coefficients, insert zero at exponent zero, and form the strict tower U by composing successors. Let v be the compatible completed uniformizer section [def-sp-completed-uniformizer-section], and suppose v^j annihilates U_j. For every n ≤ m, the map coker(v^n:U_m→U_m)→U_n induced by U_m→U_n is a quasi-isomorphism. No existence or cone-limit assertion is included.

source.place: Strict flat-model normalization: only the scalar-cokernel quasi-isomorphism field

proof.text: Compose the finite semilinear successor chain maps inductively, with the canonical restriction comparison. The successor representation equations transport the normalization Hom bijections through the representative isomorphisms. Compose universal arrows and use the exact derived-restriction comparison to obtain the universal Hom bijection for each composite. This part is proved in Lean by finiteChainComp_universal.

Naturality and associativity of restriction comparisons identify the restriction of a composite semilinear chain map with the composite of its restrictions. A proved generic sequence-map recursion then identifies these completed restrictions with the actual strict tower maps. For positive unequal exponents, apply the single-map scalar cokernel comparison to this composite and its universal Hom bijection.

At exponent zero the scalar is the identity, and both its cokernel and the inserted level zero are zero. At equal exponents the scalar vanishes by the given annihilation and the transition is the identity; its cokernel descent has the cokernel projection as inverse. Both edge cases are proved directly in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem normalizedDVR_flat_cokernel
    (T : NormalizedDVRTower l E X D hl)
    (eP : ∀ j : ℕ, (@DerivedCategory.Q _ _ _ (HasDerivedCategory.standard _)).obj
      (P j) ≅ T.M j)
    (hrep : ∀ j : ℕ,
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (g j) ≫
        (normalizedDVRModuleRes l E X j.le_succ).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app (P j) ≫
        (normalizedDVRRes l E X j.le_succ).map (eP j).hom =
      (eP (j + 1)).hom ≫ T.tau j.le_succ)
    (hflat : ∀ (j : ℕ) (i : ℤ), exactFunctor _ _
      (@MonoidalCategory.tensorRight _ _
        (SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory (integralCoefficientCommRingSheaf l E X j))
        ((P j).X i)))
    (hkflat : ∀ j : ℕ, CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (P j))
    (hzero : ∀ j : ℕ, normalizedDVRUniformizer l E X ^ j •
      𝟙 ((normalizedDVRFlatTower l E X D hl P g).obj (op j)) = 0)
    {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) :
    QuasiIso (cokernel.desc
      (normalizedDVRUniformizer l E X ^ n •
        𝟙 ((normalizedDVRFlatTower l E X D hl P g).obj (op m)))
      ((normalizedDVRFlatTower l E X D hl P g).map (homOfLE h).op) (by
        rw [Linear.smul_comp, Category.id_comp, ← Category.comp_id
          ((normalizedDVRFlatTower l E X D hl P g).map (homOfLE h).op),
          ← Linear.comp_smul, hzero n, comp_zero]))
